decisionsTitle: One elevation profile from the GPX: on the event page with the checkpoints the club ticks, previewed in the editor, and the core the race number will draw from
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-16:** on the event page he had put a picture of the elevation profile — «I would like to have a widget actually! And read it from the GPX»; «actually GPX + custom points (course points) and select which ones to show on the elevation profile»; and on the race number: «I want to show the KM & Elevation and hydration points»; then «mi-ar plăcea cumva să refolosesc acel widget … adică să fie și pe pagină și pe BIB». His screenshot: an «ALT» axis (608 / 681 / 755 / 828), a filled area, a km axis 0.00 … 9.0 KM, pins at about 3.8 / 4.5 / 6.2 km with small glyphs, a pointer line «4.5 KM», above the table «Puncte de control». Amends §718 (the route's GPX), §741 (the route section's maps) and §757 (the checkpoints: the page side).

**Decision — one core, three drawings.** `src/modules/routes/elevation/` has a pure core — `parse.ts`, `geometry.ts`, `glyphs.ts` and `pointer.ts` import nothing from `registrations/` or `content/` and know no React and no DOM (`read.ts` is the store's reader, the two `.tsx` files are the drawings) — so the event page, the editor's preview and (the next change) the race number's strip draw from the same decisions. `parse.ts` reads the GPX's `<trkpt>` (else `<rtept>`) with an `<ele>` into at most 400 points evenly by distance, the distance by haversine and the climb as the bib's own reader measures them (a test holds the two to one per cent; the bib's reader stays until the bib switches). `geometry.ts` puts everything in a box of any aspect and unit: the line and the area as **point arrays** (a PDF draws points, an SVG joins them), the kilometre scale (a tick every 1 km up to 12 km, 2 km up to 25, 5 km beyond; labels dropped where they would touch a kept label or an end word, the ticks kept), the altitude ticks (round values in steps of 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500 m …, fewer where the words would touch), the highest and lowest point's words (only the highest when the two are within `minAltitudeGapMeters`: the few-metres rule), a route that climbs under 20 m drawn flat and not stretched to the box, the markers (one per checkpoint handed in, **never dropped**: the point on the line, a glyph by kind — water, food, first aid, timing, direction, else a dot — a pin head in a band above the plot, raised a row when two heads would touch), a `compact` mode (no marker words, two altitude ticks, only the highest extreme) and `orientation: "mirrored"` (every x and every anchor flipped). Every text is a string the caller formatted through the `format` callbacks it hands in, so Romanian's «4,5» and English's «4.5» live outside the core.

**The page's chart is a Server Component, in two sizes.** `ElevationProfile.tsx` draws inline SVG from the core: the area in the theme's primary at a light wash and the line in primary (`var(--mui-palette-*)`, so both looks and both colour schemes follow, no colour literal), the «Alt» axis at the left with a faint grid, the kilometre axis at the foot with «km» once after the last label, the pins in the theme's secondary (the accent) with the kind's glyph as path data (`glyphs.ts`; no MUI icon inside an SVG, no component across the server/client boundary), `<title>` the point's name, `role="img"` with «Profilul traseului: 9,0 km, de la 608 la 828 m» and a visually hidden list of the pins. **A single viewBox was refused:** at 1000 units wide it scales a label from 11 px on a 320 px phone to 30 px on a desktop, so the page draws a narrow chart (360 × 240, labels 14 units: 11.2 px at 320) and a wide one (1000 × 280, labels 19 units: 12.7 px at 700 px and 19 px at 1000), the one that fits shown by CSS alone from 700 px — each decided by the core for its own box, so the labels dropped by crowding on a phone are the phone's. The editor's preview is the compact variant (300 × 160, labels 17 units: 11.6 px in the editor's card at a 320 px phone, where its chart is about 204 px wide, and never larger than 300 px). A test holds every label to 11 px or more as drawn and every word and pin inside its viewBox. **The room the labels need is read from what the core drew:** the altitude axis's left inset follows the widest round tick actually drawn (a route from 800 to 990 m has a «1000» tick, one digit longer than its highest altitude), and a chart with no pins keeps a line at its top for the «Alt» caption, so neither meets a tick's words; the core never prints «-0».

**The pointer is a client island over plain data** (`ElevationPointer.tsx`; §370): a finger, the mouse or the arrow keys (a hundredth of the route each, the page keys a tenth, home and end) put a line and «4,5 km · 712 m» at the nearest profile point, the name of a checkpoint within two hundred metres added; nothing before the first event, a mouse leaving takes the line away, a touch leaves it where the finger lifted, `touch-action: pan-y` keeps a vertical swipe scrolling the page, and the readout is announced politely for keys only. The arithmetic is `pointer.ts`, tested without a browser. Without scripts the static chart stands.

**The read is cached by the file's key, and a failure is never cached.** `cachedRouteElevation(eventId, gpxKey)` (`public-cache/reads.ts`) reads the GPX from the store and parses it once, keyed by the event and the file's storage key — a new upload is a new key — under the `events` tag the event page's other reads expire with; it never asks the database, so a visitor costs no wake of Neon, and never fetches the 4 MB file per visit. A file that was read is kept (with or without a profile in it); a store that fails or an object that is missing throws `ElevationUnreadable`, which the cache lets through without keeping, answered with no chart for that view and nothing else — and **the static page made without its chart is kept a minute, never a day** (`holdPageFor(DEGRADED_PAGE_SECONDS)`, §549, as every other part left out of a page), so a store's bad moment never leaves the page without its chart for a day. The read is `storeOnly` (`publicRead`'s last argument): outside the database's breaker (§447), the red month's cache-only rule and the saved copy, all of which are about sparing Neon — so a resting database never hides a chart the store can give, and a store read never resets the back-off of a database still away nor, failing with a network error, opens its breaker. The editor's preview and the draft preview read the same file straight from the store, kept in the process by the key.

**Where it stands.** In the route section, under the maps and above the file's download and the table «Puncte de control», only when the GPX parses. The table still lists **every** checkpoint; the chart pins only the ones the club left ticked. **Nothing the club uploaded is removed:** the page offers a picture of the profile only through the route description's rich text (a picture inside the text, §72–§73) — the owner's own picture stays where he put it, and whether to take it out now that the chart exists is his decision, not this change's.

**The tick.** `event_checkpoints.on_profile` (migration `0164`, `boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, expand only): on for every point written before it and for a new point; «Arată pe profilul traseului» on each point of the card «Puncte de control», saved with the row (an edit of the point, audited like any other change of the list, the tick in the audit line's `from` and `to`), carried by the event's JSON file (`onProfile`, true when a file made before it has none; **written only for a point that is off**, so a file of ticked points still reads on the release before this one, which refuses any unknown key — QA ships a day before production; the file stays version 3) and by «Duplică» and a series' dates. An unticked box posts nothing, so the form also posts a marker that it drew the box (`cp[n].onProfileShown`): **a form drawn before the box existed, saved after it, leaves a point as it was** — «not posted» is never read as «unticked», or one stale tab would take every pin off the page. The tick's own help: «Punctele debifate rămân în tabel și pe pagină; doar profilul nu le desenează.»; the preview's intro adds where the race number follows, by the labels that exist: «Numărul de concurs le arată după setarea „Punctele de control pe profil” din „Numere de concurs (BIB)”.» — the race number does not read the tick yet (its picture stamp is unchanged by it), and the next change decides whether it follows it, and then the words change there. The card also draws the preview «Așa apare pe pagină» above the rows: the saved GPX and the saved rows, drawn on the server, so it follows a save and not the typing — one sentence says so.

**The privacy notice does not change:** the chart is made from the club's own file on its own storage; no third party is asked and the visitor's address goes nowhere new.

**Refused:** one viewBox for every width; MUI icons inside the SVG; the profile stored in the database or parsed per visitor; labels on the pins of the page (the kilometre axis and the pointer say where each is; the name is the pin's title and the hidden list).
changelogLine: - **The route's elevation profile** — the event page draws the GPX's profile between the maps and the table «Puncte de control» (axes, area, a pin with its glyph for each checkpoint the club ticks «Arată pe profilul traseului», a pointer that reads the kilometre and the altitude), the editor's card previews it, and the shared core is what the race number will draw from. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 77. Given an event whose route has a GPX with altitudes, when its page renders, then between the route's maps and the table «Puncte de control» stands the elevation profile — the area and the line, an «Alt» axis, a kilometre axis with «km» once, one pin with the glyph of its kind for each checkpoint ticked «Arată pe profilul traseului» and none for an unticked one, which the table still lists — with an accessible name «Profilul traseului: 9,0 km, de la 608 la 828 m» and a hidden list of its pins; its labels are 11 pixels or more at 320 pixels, a narrow chart and a wide one are drawn and CSS shows the one that fits, a file with no altitudes or an unreadable store leaves the chart out and nothing else, and a pointer, a finger or the arrow keys read «4,5 km · 712 m» and the name of a point within two hundred metres, the readout staying inside the chart's width at 320 pixels (2026-10-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 140. Given the card «Puncte de control», then each point has the tick «Arată pe profilul traseului» (on for a new point and for every point saved before it), saved with the row and audited as an edit; the card draws above its rows the preview «Așa apare pe pagină» — the page's chart from the saved GPX and the saved rows, refreshed by a save and not by typing, its labels 11 pixels or more at 320 pixels — and, beside the tick, the sentence that unticked points stay in the table and on the page; a form drawn before the tick existed leaves a point's tick as it was, and the event's JSON file carries `onProfile` (true when absent) through an export, an import as new and an import over an event (2026-10-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: one elevation profile from the GPX: on the event page with the checkpoints the club ticks, previewed in the editor; the core the race number will draw from
